author: Mark Atwood
text:
Items 2, 3 and 7 also fixed.

2. pkix-revocation-http's README showed an API that never existed: fetch(&self, url: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, _> and HttpCrlFetcher::new with two arguments. The real trait is fetch(&self, req: &FetchRequest<'_>) -> Result<FetchResponse, FetchError> and new takes (fetcher, verifier, now_unix). Rewrote the example against the shipped signatures, including the FetchError::Transport boxing and the FetchResponse fields, then dropped the 'Planned API' heading -- which, as the bead noted, was the only thing warning a reader the snippet was fiction. Also carried over the now_unix-is-fixed-for-the-life-of-the-fetcher caveat from the rustdoc, since that is the mistake the example would otherwise invite.

3. The bead said the Placeholder list 'still legitimately holds PKCS#11'. It does not any more -- pkix-truststore-pkcs11 0.1.2 is published, as is pkix-truststore-system 0.2.1, both verified against crates.io. So the whole section was stale, not half of it. It is now 'Adapter crates that ship', with links.

7. Resolved by deleting the duplicate rather than reconciling two copies. pkix-truststore now points at pkix-truststore-pkcs11 for which tokens are covered, and says why the list is not repeated. The pkcs11 README became the canonical version: it gained TPM 2.0 and SoftHSM from the pkix-truststore copy, kept OpenSC / CAC / FIPS-mode, stopped saying 'Planned support' for a published crate, and now says any PKCS#11 C_GetFunctionList provider should work with the named ones being what it was checked against -- which is the honest shape for a vendor list.

Still open: 1 (verify the SSRF three-way drift is fully closed), 5 (baseline-limbo-analysis stale tc60 bullet), 6 (re-classify the PKITS per-bucket breakdowns), 8, 9, 10, 11 (drifted duplicates needing a canonical version), and the heading-style call.
